name: Floreo
one_liner: Virtual-reality lessons for autistic and other neurodivergent children and adults to practise social, safety and daily-living skills with a guide.
best_for: Autistic children, teens and adults practising social and safety skills with a parent, teacher or therapist
Families, schools and clinics wanting repeatable practice for situations that are hard to stage in real life
not_for: Anyone in crisis or thinking about suicide: call or text 988
Anyone who cannot use a VR headset comfortably (motion sickness, sensory distress)
Anyone looking for a replacement for a full therapy program such as ABA or speech therapy
short_description: Guided VR lessons for autistic and neurodivergent learners to practise social, communication, safety and daily-living skills.
long_description: Floreo is a virtual-reality learning program for neurodivergent people of all ages, especially autistic learners. The learner practises situations in a headset (social greetings, joint attention, street safety, interacting with police, calming strategies) while a guide such as a parent, teacher, behaviour analyst or speech therapist runs and adjusts the lesson from a separate phone or tablet. A family subscription for one learner starts at $69.99 a month, with the headset separate; schools and clinics have tiered pricing. Medicaid waiver programs in some states, including Tennessee, New York, Wisconsin and North Carolina, reimburse it. A 2026 randomized trial of its police-safety module found modest short-term gains compared with a video program. A prescription version, FloreoRx, was submitted to the FDA for De Novo review in April 2026 and is not yet authorized.
patient_summary: The learner wears a VR headset and practises real-world situations, such as greeting people, crossing a street or talking with a police officer, while a parent, teacher or therapist guides the lesson from a phone or tablet. Families can subscribe directly, and some state Medicaid waivers, schools and clinics pay for it.

pricing.notes: Headset sold separately. School and clinic pricing is tiered by number of students and length. Reimbursed by Medicaid waivers in some states (TN, NY, WI, NC); a Category III CPT code (0770T) exists, but private insurance coverage varies. HSA/FSA use may be possible; check with your provider.

privacy.notes: Says it does not sell personal information or use learner data for advertising, and acts as a HIPAA business associate in healthcare settings; a deletion right for all users is not clearly stated.

faqs.a: Floreo VR is a virtual reality therapy tool for neurodivergent individuals that teaches social, communication, behavioral, and daily life skills through immersive lessons designed by educators and clinicians.
Floreo is designed for neurodivergent individuals of all ages, including those with autism, ADHD, PTSD, and anxiety who need to develop social, communication, and life skills.

Floreo subscriptions cost approximately $50 per student per month. VR headsets can be purchased separately or bundled, and qualifying school districts may receive free Meta Quest headsets through Meta's donation program.

A learner wears a VR headset to experience immersive lessons while a coach monitors in real-time via a paired device. The VR environments allow safe practice of skills that are difficult to create naturally.

citation.authors: Solorzano R, Turnacioglu S, Ravindran V, et al. (author order not verified)
citation.title: Virtual Reality Intervention to Empower Autistic People to Interact With Police: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial for Autistic Teens and Adults
citation.journal: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders

clinical_trials.outcome: Reduced fidgeting during live police interactions vs control; other improvements not significantly different between groups. Several authors are Floreo employees.
clinical_trials.study_design: Randomized controlled trial vs video-based program (BeSAFE)

availability.note: Sold to families, schools and clinics; Medicaid waiver reimbursement in some states. FloreoRx (prescription version) is under FDA review.
